The complete Megenberg II25 effects unit93.8–32 connects ocular-medium damage with sight, tender plant organs with purposive covering, burning hair with an uninjured body, and a surviving mother with a dependent child's mediated death. Each causal account keeps its own recipient, mechanism, modality and outcome; no general shared immunity or single damage mechanism follows.

design.mechanism: The text gives a connected sequence of selective effects without one universal mechanism. A person looking directly at lightning can be blinded because the crystalline moisture in the eyeball, which bears visual power, burns. Blossoms are damaged, especially tender vine blossoms, therefore nature provides protective leaves around fruit-bearing buds, like a nurse wrapping a child, and broad vine leaves to cover grapes. Hair may burn without injury to its bearer: vapour lacks sufficient force to harm the person but burning, rapid movement burns dry soft hair. The following Marcia story preserves maternal survival and fetal death, explained instead through the child's weakness and the mother's fright tearing its binding bands, whose tearing also tears the child's veins and heart. Distinct affected objects and explanatory routes must stay attached to their own consequences.
design.prediction: A faithful complete account must allow bodily survival to coexist with loss in a part or dependent recipient. The hair's burning is not the body's injury; the mother's absence of harm is not the child's survival. Ocular damage explains loss of sight through the named medium, whereas plant covering is a stated protective purpose with a nurse analogy, not a reported successful medical intervention. Swapping the damaged medium, the surviving bearer or the owner of fright changes the written consequences. Mere lists of eye, leaf, hair and child erase why outcomes differ.
design.contrast: R1: one strike imposes the same harm/survival state on every associated object. R2: all soft things are immune because the preceding hard/soft comparison gives less damage to soft things. R3: maternal fright is the same literal burning mechanism as hair damage. R4: leaves demonstrably guarantee survival, or the nurse analogy commands human treatment. R5: the woman is physically torn while the child is spared, reversing owners. R6: quick motion entails enough force to injure the body, erasing the source's distinction between insufficient bodily force and rapid burning movement.
whole_source_duties: 93.8–12: retain often, direct looking at lightning, burning of crystalline moisture in the eyeball, and visual power located there. Blindness has the source's named intermediary; it is a historical claim, not modern guidance.

93.12–19: retain damage to blossoms and especially tender vine blossoms, fruit-bearing buds covered by leaves, nurse/child/swaddling comparison, and the vine's broad leaves covering grapes against lightning. The source gives nature's protective purpose, not measured efficacy, guaranteed immunity or an instruction to a human nurse/physician.

93.19–25: retain hair under the armpits and elsewhere, often burning without bodily harm, insufficient force to injure the person, burning rapid movement around the person, and dry soft hair. Rapid and forceful are not silently made one measured variable; no numerical threshold is supplied.

93.25–32: retain named Marcia, a Roman princely woman, being struck, her unborn child's death and her own lack of harm. Preserve the child still weak, the mother's fright, tearing of the bands binding the child, and that same tearing damaging the child's veins and heart. No unsupported identification of those bands with a modern named organ; no medical truth claim.

The Marcia continuation is introduced by alsô, linking selective outcome to the preceding account, but supplies a different proposed mechanism. It is not a second observation establishing identical vapour-burning causation or a controlled paired trial.
The local sequence enumerates first/second/third effects, then adds the Marcia story. It does not enumerate four parallel classes, four actors or four seasons; no figure map follows.

Preceding92.23–30 says hard bodies such as steel/rock/stone block vapour and break/split, while soft things suffer less; a sword and untranslated spæn break while sheath leather remains whole. Less harm is not universal soft-body immunity. This context must not erase the explicit dry soft hair burning in the focal unit.

Following93.32–94.1 is the separately retained596 claim and criticism of advance-warning immunity; it is outside this local scope and does not guarantee protection here. Following94.1–7 also reports human non-universal death versus trees/animals and especially eagle/laurel damage; retain its attribution/tension without silently reversing the source to canonical immunity.
